title: War of the chatbots: Bard, Bing Chat, ChatGPT, Ernie and beyond. The new AI gold rush and its impact on higher education
extended_summary:
This paper examines the rapid rise of large language model chatbots—especially ChatGPT, Bing Chat, Bard, and Baidu’s Ernie—and their implications for higher education. The central problem is that generative AI is advancing quickly enough to affect teaching, assessment, academic integrity, and institutional policy, while also creating risks such as hallucinations, misinformation, privacy concerns, and deceptive or biased outputs.

Rather than presenting a primary experiment on learners, the article offers a comparative, critical review of major chatbot systems and a synthesis of the emerging English- and Chinese-language literature on chatbots in higher education. The authors describe the corporate background of major systems, summarize their capabilities and shortcomings, and discuss how these tools are being used or considered by students and instructors in higher education contexts. They also note the limits and risks of current systems, including inaccurate answers, hallucinations, lack of reliable sourcing, jailbreakability, and censorship-related constraints in China.

The paper’s conclusions are largely precautionary. It argues that current chatbots are powerful but still fall short of the sensational claims made about them, and that higher education should respond through assessment redesign, careful teaching practices, student guidance, and institutional policy changes. The article does not report a K–12 intervention or empirical study of coaching or lesson-plan feedback; instead, it is a theoretical and review-oriented discussion centered on higher education.

identified_tools.name: ChatGPT
identified_tools.description: OpenAI's GPT-based conversational AI chatbot/LLM system used for generating, summarizing, and answering text prompts.
identified_tools.use_case: This paper reviews and compares ChatGPT (GPT-3.5 and GPT-4) as one of several major LLM-based chatbots relevant to higher education, discussing its capabilities, limitations, and risks.

findings.finding_summary: The paper synthesizes prior literature and notes that ChatGPT has substantial potential for higher-education uses, but also major weaknesses including hallucinations, outdated knowledge, unreliable reasoning, and ease of jailbreaking. It cites claims that GPT-4 outperforms GPT-3.5 on tests such as the UBE and AP exams, while also emphasizing concerns about misinformation and academic integrity.
findings.measure: Narrative review of reported capabilities, limitations, and test-performance claims in prior studies

quality_tier_rationale: This is a narrative review/article rather than an empirical evaluation, and the paper itself does not report original outcome data for ChatGPT. The evidence presented is secondary and descriptive.
impact_tier_rationale: The paper describes potentially substantial effects on assessment and teaching, but without primary effect estimates from this article. Because the synthesis highlights both benefits and serious harms/limitations, the net impact is unclear.
